text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele is continuing his visit to the U.S.

- Leading party Latvia's Way held its conference on September 22. The party believes local governments in the districts should be abolished and their functions handed over to lower municipalities and the central government. But it opposes the idea that district administrators should be appointed by the government cabinet.

- Speaking at the conference the head of the Latvia's Way parliamentary faction, Andrei Panteleyev, said the party should evaluate the activities of the former interior minister Janis Adamsons for not observing voting discipline recently.

- Four Latvian TV firms want to annul the licence of Latvian Independent TV, which has been broadcasting instead of the Russian Ostankino TV since August 29, as well as organise a new tender for the right to broadcast on the third channel. They claim the company breached the Radio and TV law. The position of the Latvian Radio and TV Council is to be announced today.

- The Association of Local Governments has carried out a poll among its members to find out whether they are ready to start the winter heating season. Of 238 municipalities polled 138 acknowledged they would have problems.
- President Guntis Ulmanis is planning to visit Russia in spring next year.
- Since August 1, 7.1 percent of Latvia's active population has been officially registered as searching for a job.
- A Riga police department which deals with searching for stolen cars is to be re-organised and re-manned because of suspicions its personnel were linked with criminals.

- Valery Machugin, vice-president of one of Latvia's largest holding companies, Mono, was shot dead yesterday in the yard of his house together with his girl-friend, a well-known photo model. The woman was badly wounded.
- The film forum Arsenal ended yesterday.
- According to data of the Latvian Association of Commercial banks, in August the assets of Latvian banks increased by 4.3 percent to achieve 964.098 million lats.
- Former prime minister Maris Gailis may be appointed chief manager of the Riga port.
